query:
*[_type == "society" && listed != false] | order(name asc){
    _id,
    name,
    "slug": slug.current,
    province,
    region,
    founded,
    meets,
    venue,
    memberCount,
    description,
    logo,
    website,
    markBadge,
    contactEmail,
    contactPhone,
    committee[]{ role, name },
    facebookUrl,
    instagramUrl,
    annualShow,
    foundedPlaceholder,
    memberCountPlaceholder,
    meetPlaceholder,
    venuePlaceholder
  }

result.description: Founded in 1957, the Cape Orchid Society is the oldest orchid group in South Africa and a founder member of the South African Orchid Council. The COS strives to bring together those interested in orchids in order to promote and encourage the culture and conservation of orchids, as well as to educate and provide a base for all other orchid-related activities. The COS began with monthly meetings, which still continue today, providing informative presentations, practical growing advice and an opportunity for growers to display and discuss their plants and flowers. The Society hosts a number of events throughout the year, including two shows in which growers showcase their blooms, an auction, greenhouse open days and hikes. We also provide members with a newsletter, monthly guest speakers, local judging, and much, much, more!

result.description: Gonubie Orchid Society was formed in 1998 by Eric Dodd and became affiliated to SAOC in May 1999. The Society first met at Pioneer Nursery in Gonubie. In 2014, the Society moved their meetings to the Gonubie Hotel. The Society has always been a strong Society and is well known for it’s yearly Orchid Shows. It’s membership has been strong with an average of 30 members since it’s establishment. Since May 2026, we meet at the Beacon Bay Bowling Club.

result.description: The Northern Gauteng Orchid Society (NGOS), formerly the Orchid Society of Northern Transvaal (ONT) was founded in 1967 and is the fourth oldest orchid society in South Africa. Based in Pretoria, it serves the Northern Gauteng and adjacent region. The society’s emblem is Angraecum stella-africae.
